To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TTTD and ATTD of P were not affected by phytase supplementation in triticale-DDGS diets.
phytase supplementation increased the ATTD of phosphorus in triticale dried grains with solubes but did not affect the TTTD.
the TTTD value for P of triticale DGS was 75.5% in pigs, which was increased by 5.7% when 500 FTU phytase was added per kilogram of diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the TTTD and digestibility response of pigs to phytate phosphorus in triticale DGS.
the P bioavailability of triticale and triticale DDGs.
the P utilization of triticale-based DDGS by growing pigs and the effects of phytase supplementation on P utilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TTTD and ATTD of P were not significantly different between triticale DDGs without and with supplemental phytase.
the TTTD (75.4%) of P in triticle DDGS was similar to the ATTD of 75.7% when phytase was added at 500 FTUs/kg.
the TTTD (75.4%) of P in triticle DDGS was similar to the ATTD (77.3%) of P in diets supplemented with 500 FTU of phytase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TTTD and ATTD of P from DDGS are similar and are affected by phytase supplementation in a similar manner.
phytase supplementation to diets containing triticale DDGs increased the apparent digestibility of P, but not the true digestibility.
the TTTD and ATTD of P were 75.4 and 77.3% for triticales DDGS without phytase supplementation, and 81.1 and 76.5% with phytase supplementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TTTD values of P in triticle DDGS with or without added phytases were similar.
phytase supplementation in triticale-based diets for pigs could be beneficial for P utilization.
phytase supplementation in triticale-based diets could be used to improve P digestibility and reduce P excretion in pigs.
